recent_posts.title: Now Available: Monthly Subscriptions with a 12-Month Commitment
recent_posts.summary: Apple is introducing a new subscription payment option on the App Store: monthly subscriptions with a 12-month commitment. This lets developers offer more affordable pricing while locking users into a year-long plan. Users can cancel anytime but must complete their committed payments. Transparency features include payment tracking in Apple Account and renewal reminders via email and push notifications. Developers can configure and test this in App Store Connect and Xcode starting today. The feature will be available globally (excluding the US and Singapore) with iOS/iPadOS/macOS/visionOS 26.5 in May.

recent_posts.title: How Lykke Studios crafted the physics and feel of puffies. for Apple Arcade
recent_posts.summary: Lykke Studios, the team behind Apple Design Award winners stitch. and tint., shares the development story behind puffies. — a puzzle game built around virtual puffy stickers available on Apple Arcade. The 8-person team spent months perfecting physics interactions, haptic feedback, snap distances, and accessibility features. Every one of the game's 4,000 stickers is a 3D-modeled object governed by a physics engine, and the team scrapped entire codebases to get interactions feeling right. The studio's philosophy centers on craft over speed, with no automated level design and a strong focus on inclusivity features.

recent_posts.title: How Infold Games fashioned an open world for Infinity Nikki
recent_posts.summary: Infold Games shares the technical and artistic decisions behind Infinity Nikki, an open-world RPG and 2025 Apple Design Award winner for Visuals and Graphics. The team of ~800 discusses their custom fabric material system using four-layer UV blending textures, a proprietary jewelry rendering system with complex refraction and 3S light transmission, and physical simulation using skeletal chain algorithms and Chaos Cloth. They also explain how they worked around Unreal Engine 5's motion blur interference on UV animations to achieve animated outfit patterns, and how constraint-based algorithms replaced collision-based ones for stable cloth physics across platforms.

recent_posts.title: Q&A: How Plane Finder set itself up for the long haul
recent_posts.summary: Plane Finder founders Jodie and Lee Armstrong share how they built a global flight-tracking business with a team of just eight people by going all-in on Apple's native ecosystem since 2009. They discuss their early adoption philosophy, reliance on MapKit, Metal, and StoreKit 2, their approach to Liquid Glass, and how they grew a worldwide network of self-manufactured flight receivers by leveraging their app's user base. They also hint at upcoming UI changes under the codename 'Plane Finder Double Glazed' and plans to explore machine learning.

recent_posts.title: App Store expands support to 11 new languages
recent_posts.summary: App Store Connect now supports localized metadata for 11 new languages, bringing the total to 50 supported localizations. The newly added languages are Bangla, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Slovenian, Tamil, Telugu, and Urdu — with a focus on expanding reach in India. Developers can provide localized app names, descriptions, screenshots, and more, and can use new localized App Store badges in marketing materials starting with their next version submission.

recent_posts.title: Updated Apple Developer Program License Agreement now available
recent_posts.summary: Apple has updated its Developer Program License Agreement with changes effective March 30, 2026. Key updates include specified requirements for the Foveated Streaming framework with clarified data privacy requirements, requirements for the Family Controls framework, and requirements for the Accessory Notifications and Accessory Live Activities frameworks. Developers must sign in to their accounts to accept the updated terms. Translated versions will be available within one month.

recent_posts.title: Update on regulated medical device apps in the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, and United States
recent_posts.summary: Apple is updating App Store requirements for health and medical apps distributed in the EEA, UK, and US. Starting now, new apps in the Health & Fitness or Medical categories — or those flagged for medical content in the Age Rating questionnaire — must declare their regulated medical device status in App Store Connect. Existing apps have until early 2027 to comply, after which failure to declare status will block app updates. The App Store will display this status on product pages to improve transparency for users.

recent_posts.title: Adjustments to the China storefront of the App Store on iOS and iPadOS
recent_posts.summary: Apple is reducing App Store commission rates for the China mainland storefront effective March 15, 2026. The standard commission for In-App Purchase and paid app transactions drops from 30% to 25%. Qualifying transactions under the Small Business Program, Mini Apps Partner Program, and auto-renewals of subscriptions after the first year will drop from 15% to 12%. Developers do not need to sign updated terms by March 15 to benefit from the new rates. The Apple Developer Program License Agreement has been revised accordingly.

recent_posts.title: Updated App Review Guidelines now available
recent_posts.summary: Apple has updated its App Review Guidelines to explicitly state that apps featuring random or anonymous chat functionality must comply with the User-Generated Content guideline (section 1.2). Translated versions of the updated guidelines will be available on the Apple Developer website within one month.

recent_posts.title: Swift Student Challenge submissions are now open
recent_posts.summary: Apple's Swift Student Challenge is accepting submissions through February 28, 2026. Students worldwide can submit app playgrounds on any topic, with no prior experience required. Participants need only a Mac or iPad with Xcode or Swift Playground, and submissions should be experienceable within 3 minutes. The challenge is free to enter and offers learning resources and guidance from past winners.

top_posts.summary: Join us for a special Apple event on September 12 at 10 a.m. PT. Watch it live at apple.com.com.

top_posts.title: Hello Developer: January 2026
top_posts.summary: Apple's January 2026 developer newsletter highlights a SwiftUI activity in Cupertino, expanded Liquid Glass resources, a video overview of Apple design tools, new Develop in Swift tutorials, and an article on leveraging foundation models. The update provides developers with learning opportunities and resources across Apple's development ecosystem.

top_posts.title: Code new worlds
top_posts.summary: Be among the first to learn the latest about Apple platforms, technologies, and tools. Join the developer community for an in-depth look at the future of Apple platforms. Watch on the web or in the Apple Developer app for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple TV.

top_posts.title: Hello Developer: February 2026
top_posts.summary: Apple announces agentic coding capabilities coming to Xcode, alongside upcoming developer events including a code-along session on coding intelligence and the Swift Student Challenge. The update also highlights new learning resources covering SwiftUI, design, and security topics for Apple platform developers.

top_posts.title: iOS and iPadOS 26 design kits are here
top_posts.summary: Apple has released official UI design kits for iOS and iPadOS 26, making them available for both Figma and Sketch design tools. These design resources help developers and designers create apps that follow Apple's latest design guidelines and interface standards.
